en: III · Historical Materialism

O gentlemen, the time of life is short …
An if we live, we live to tread on kings
— William Shakespeare
zh:
啊，诸位先生，人生苦短……
若我们活着，便是为践踏君王而活
——威廉·莎士比亚

en: The concept of labour-power, though it recurs in every turn of phrase throughout economic and sociological analysis, has itself hardly been thought about at all. Professional philosophers shrug their shoulders at the thought of doing so, and at most busy themselves with themes which are only its corollary (biopolitics, for example). And yet this concept, which is apparently self-evident and even superficial, is very much tangled up with our study of historical time.
zh: 劳动力概念虽然在经济学和社会学分析的每一种措辞中反复出现，却几乎从未真正得到思考。职业哲学家一想到要思考它就耸耸肩，至多忙于处理只是其推论的主题，例如生命政治（biopolitics）。然而，这个看似不证自明、甚至肤浅的概念，同我们对历史时间的研究有着千丝万缕的纠葛。

en: The capitalist production relation is based on the difference between labour-power and effective labour. Labour-power is pure potential, very much different from the corresponding acts: ‘When we speak of capacity for labour, we do not speak of labour, any more than when we speak of capacity for digestion, we speak of digestion.’
However, it is a potential with the very concrete prerogatives of a commodity; of a not-now which is subject to supply and demand. The capitalist buys the production
as such (‘the aggregate of those mental and physical capabilities existing in a human being’, Marx writes

), and not one or several determinate performances of this faculty. After this purchase has taken place, the capitalist can employ the commodity which he now possesses as he pleases: ‘The purchaser of labour-power consumes it by setting the seller of it to work. By working, the latter
becomes actually, what before he only was potentially.’

The really-supplied labour does not only reimburse the capitalist for the previous outlay of money – through which he obtained the other person’s labour-power – but continues for a supplementary lapse of time: and here lies the genesis of surplus-value, the enigma of capitalist accumulation.
zh: 资本主义生产关系以劳动力与现实劳动之间的差异为基础。劳动力是纯粹潜能，同相应实现截然不同：‘当我们谈论劳动能力时，我们并不是在谈论劳动，正如谈论消化能力并不是在谈论消化。’
然而，这是一种具有商品的极其具体的属性的潜能，是受供求支配的非现在。资本家购买的是生产官能本身——马克思写道，是‘存在于人的身体中的体力和智力的总和’
——而不是这一官能的一项或若干确定实行。购买发生之后，资本家便可以随意使用现在由他占有的商品：‘劳动力的购买者通过让劳动力的出卖者劳动来消费劳动力。后者通过劳动，现实地成为他此前只潜在地所是的东西。’
实际提供的劳动不仅偿付资本家此前为取得他人劳动力所预付的货币，而且还会延续一段额外时间；剩余价值由此产生，这正是资本主义积累之谜。

en: This synthesis is rather incomplete, certainly. No worry: its only purpose is immediately to demonstrate the

that historical materialism has to get to the bottom of. We know that the discrepancy between act and potential, ‘now’ and not-now’, presence and non-actuality, is the root of history in general. With capitalism, however, this discrepancy (in the detailed version of it provided by the labour-power/labour couple) attains extraordinary empirical, pragmatic and economic significance. In sum, it itself becomes a

. We ought to conclude that capitalism is the epoch in which the condition of possibility of history appears in the guise of one phenomenon among others, even constituting the fulcrum of a specific mode of production; the epoch in which the
of experience can be experienced

. The analogy with the Christian Revelation is striking: a presupposition which was at first hidden is now incarnated with tangible features, exposed to the most immediate perception. What appears with worldly, contingent features is not, it should be understood, anything atemporal, but precisely and only the
of historical time, its hidden structure. This epiphany does not redeem: rather, the manner in which
it takes place is the opposite of salvation. We have to bear a Revelation without a Messiah.
zh: 这项概括当然相当不完整。但无妨，它唯一的目的，是立即展示历史唯物主义必须彻底弄清的时间悖论。我们知道，实现与潜能、‘现在’与非现在、在场与非现实性之间的差异，是一般历史的根源。然而在资本主义中，这一差异——具体体现为劳动力／劳动这一对——取得非凡的经验、实践和经济意义。总之，它本身成为一个历史事实。我们应当得出结论：资本主义是这样一个时代，历史之可能性条件以诸现象之一的面貌出现，甚至构成一种特定生产方式的支点；在这个时代，经验的历史性能够被历史地经验。它同基督教启示的类比十分鲜明：起初隐蔽的前提，如今以可触摸的特征取得肉身，暴露在最直接的知觉之下。当然，以世俗而偶然的面貌显现的并非某种无时间之物，而恰恰只是历史时间的纹理及其隐蔽结构。这场显现并不救赎；相反，它发生的方式正是救赎的反面。我们不得不承受一场没有弥赛亚的启示。
卡尔·马克思，《资本论》第一卷，第6章，marxists.org。
